column17: Not a provider but the software most of this roster runs, so its mechanics bound what any of them can promise. Per-subscriber hard USD caps are enforced before the request, in SubscriptionService.ValidateAndCheckLimits (subscription_service.go:1005), called from the api_key_auth middleware at api_key_auth.go:239 and :247. CORRECTED 2026-10-07: this cell read 'user_subscription.go CheckUsageLimits' as the pre-request path. CheckUsageLimits exists at subscription_service.go:989 but grep finds only its own definition and no caller, so it is dead code; the live path is ValidateAndCheckLimits, and CheckMonthlyLimit is its innermost predicate. There is NO proportional seat-sharing anywhere in the codebase: grep for seat/Carpool/proportional over backend/ returns only OAuth fingerprint tests. A subscriber's share is an operator-chosen dollar allowance, not a computed fraction of a seat. Recorded failure modes: (1) silent model substitution and tool-call degradation - issue 7503 attributes it to the gateway's TLS fingerprint; (2) weekly quota shrinkage under pooling - issues 5692 (24 comments) and 5786, where accounts normal on official Codex lose quota after being pooled; (3) ban risk - issues 1141, 3624, 3896, 6134, 6180, 6755, 6892; (4) availability storms - issues 6739 (49 comments), 593. GitHub reported 3,570 open issues+PRs on 2026-10-06, of which 2,625 were issues and 945 pull requests; on 2026-10-07 the combined counter read 3,571, so the pair moves by one in a day and neither number measures anything about the project.
